sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors

items.q: The structural and functional thyroid unit is the ___, with ___ in its lumen.
items.exp: The figure shows follicular epithelial cells surrounding colloid; the follicle is the functional and structural unit. (Book p899)

items.q: Match the following source developmental milestones — 1) Thyroglobulin appearance 2) Hormone synthesis begins 3) Initial gland formation … A) 29th day B) 11th week C) 3rd–4th week
items.exp: The page gives thyroglobulin by day 29 and synthesis by week 11; initial gland formation is earlier in the chapter. (Book p899)

items.q: Assess: I Parafollicular cells supply the main thyroglobulin-derived T3/T4 pool. II Thyroglobulin is a hormone precursor in the follicular system.
items.exp: Follicular cells make thyroglobulin and thyroid hormones; parafollicular C cells instead secrete calcitonin. (Book p899)

items.q: Parafollicular C cells secrete ___ rather than T3 and T4.
items.exp: The C-cell note specifically identifies calcitonin secretion. (Book p899)

items.q: A student uses this page's classical embryology scheme to trace parafollicular cells. Which association matches that scheme?
opts: Ultimobranchial body and caudal pharyngeal-pouch complex
First pharyngeal arch and Meckel cartilage
Dorsal pancreatic bud and neural tube
items.exp: The source describes ultimobranchial/neural-crest and partial fifth-pouch origin. This is a classical teaching model; modern mammalian lineage evidence supports endodermal C-cell origins rather than an unqualified neural-crest claim. (Book p899)

items.q: Match the following regulatory levels — 1) Hypothalamus 2) Pituitary 3) Thyroid follicle … A) T3/T4 B) TRH C) TSH
items.exp: The positive axis is hypothalamic TRH → pituitary TSH → thyroid T3/T4 production. (Book p899)

items.q: A patient with hypopituitarism has low free T4 and a TSH within the laboratory range. Which interpretation is best?
opts: Central hypothyroidism with an inappropriately normal TSH
Primary hypothyroidism with an appropriate TSH response
Normal thyroid function maintained by basal synthesis
Primary thyrotoxicosis with pituitary TSH suppression
items.exp: A source claim about basal synthesis does not exclude central hypothyroidism. Low or inappropriately normal TSH with low free T4 requires evaluation. (Book p899)

items.q: Match the following developmental factors — 1) TTF-1 2) PAX8 3) PROP1 … A) Choreoathetosis association B) Congenital hypothyroidism C) Combined pituitary hormone deficiency
items.exp: The table pairs TTF-1 with choreoathetosis, PAX8 with congenital hypothyroidism and PROP1 with combined pituitary deficiency. (Book p899)

items.q: Congenital hypothyroidism is accompanied by a developmental cleft abnormality in the source table. Which factor is implicated?
items.exp: TTF-2 is linked to thyroid dysgenesis and a cleft entry. The page says 'cleft thyroid'; the recognized FOXE1-associated syndrome includes cleft palate, so the literal label is imprecise. (Book p899)

items.q: A child with congenital thyroid dysfunction also has choreoathetotic movements. Which developmental gene association is most relevant?
items.exp: The TTF-1 row highlights choreoathetosis; it is distinct from the PAX8 and pituitary PROP1 associations. (Book p899)

items.q: Which is the odd one out for a primary thyroid-development factor in this table?
items.exp: PROP1 is paired with combined pituitary hormone deficiency, unlike the thyroid-development entries. (Book p899)

items.q: Evaluate the final dysgenesis note: I Thyroid dysgenesis can cause congenital hypothyroidism. II Most cases must be proven TTF-1 or TTF-2 mutations because those factors are named.
items.exp: The source links these factors to dysgenesis but its causal/frequency wording is confused. Naming genes does not establish that they explain most cases of congenital hypothyroidism. (Book p899)
